title: Harish Chandra v. State of U.P. (electricity-dues citation; para 6.8 remittal)
coram: Surya Prakash Kesarwani, J.; Jayant Banerji, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; liberty to file para 6.8 objection with stay of coercive action.
headnote: Without deciding merits, the Court disposed of a writ against a Tehsildar electricity-dues citation and two demand notices, granting liberty to object under Para 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, with a time-bound hearing and a short stay of coercive recovery.
facts: Harish Chandra approached the Allahabad High Court seeking certiorari to quash a Tehsildar, Basti citation dated 20 June 2022 demanding Rs. 1,56,513 as electricity dues, and demand notices dated 24 February 2021 (letters 750 and 751) requiring deposit of Rs. 1,27,309 and Rs. 29,144. Counsel for the power distribution corporation stated on instructions that the petitioner could file an objection to the impugned demand, to be decided in accordance with law within a time-bound period.

holding_units.holding: Without expressing any opinion on merits, the writ is disposed of with liberty to submit an objection under Para 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before respondent No. 2 within four weeks; if so submitted, it shall be decided in accordance with law within the next four weeks after reasonable opportunity of hearing. No coercive action on the impugned demand for eight weeks or until disposal of the objection, whichever is earlier.

principle_tags.application: Writ against electricity-dues citation and demand notices disposed by relegating the consumer to a Para 6.8 objection, to be decided in accordance with law after hearing, without any merits ruling on the demand.
Court directed a time-bound Para 6.8 objection and barred coercive recovery for eight weeks or until that objection is decided, whichever is earlier.

not_decided.point: merits of the electricity-dues citation and demand notices
not_decided.note: Court expressly declined to express any opinion on the merits of the petitioner's case.
